title: Hanuma meets Sri Rama
introduction: Hanuma, at the behest of Sugreeva, approaches Rama and Lakshmana in the guise of an ascetic. The reason to change his original form to that of a sanyasi is that, the intruders in this area Rama and Lakshmana appear in a self-contradictory personage. By their body built, striking features, wielding armoury they look like kings or emperors. But when it comes to their dress and hairdo, they are almost like hermits. Sugreeva is well aware of political milieu and enemy's tactics, and thus asked Hanuma not to approach them in his original monkey form in earlier chapter. Equally well, Rama and Lakshmana doubt the entry of an ascetic i.e., Hanuma in that guise, into this uninhabited place, and they wait cautiously till Hanuma reveals himself. From here up to Sundara Kanda, Hanuma's words and actions are weighted, and need an in-depth study. In this episode, what all Hanuma says is drawn from scriptures and political science, and what all Rama analyses Hanuma, by way of Hanuma's expressiveness, is relevant to scriptures, i.e., Veda-s. In mythology, Hanuma is taken as the veda vedaanga paarangataH, knower of all Vedas, and their subsidiary scriptures, nava vyaakarana panditaH, scholar in nine schools of grammars, buddhimata variSTaH , cleverest of the clever. He is the supreme scholar, teacher, and the cleverest.
closing: The research scholars point out that these many verses are not there in some ancient manuscripts and only the following verses are available. Even the tailor-made Baroda edition ends at verse 4-3-27. The above aspects of Rama's analysis etc., is available in the Eastern and Gorakhpur and other untailored manuscripts. There is an extensive commentary on these so-called extra verses, rendered in a rare commentary Dharmaakuutam dating back to 1600's, and even in earlier commentaries. The verses found in ancient manuscripts are said to be this one and half stanzas:

Taking clue of the last foot, namely vākyajnam etc., and to glorify Hanuma through the tongue of Rama, these verses from 4-3-28 to 4-3-35, are said to be crafted later, without throwing light on when and where. Rama is going to give ācārya , Teacher status to Hanuma to educate the innate soul - Seetha in Lanka - about the Almighty. So, to receive that status, according to Vaishnavaite stipulates, a guru should possess certain qualities like:

A teacher is to be well-equipped with all Veda-s, a devotee of Vishnu, always purified by hymnal purity, devotion to his own teacher, knower of mythologies, in particular, and one who is endowed with these qualities alone is called the Guru.
And Hanuma is one such according to popular belief, though not from the viewpoints of researches. It is therefore unclear whether the modern day researchers are right or the ancient commentators.
इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये किष्किन्ध काण्डे तृतियः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 3rd chapter in Kishkindha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
वचो विज्ञाय हनुमान् सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः |
पर्वतात् ऋष्यमूकात् तु पुप्लुवे यत्र राघवौ
verses.iast:
vaco vijñāya hanumān sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ |
parvatāt ṛṣyamūkāt tu pupluve yatra rāghavau
verses.translation: Mindful of the words of noble-souled Sugreeva, Hanuma took his flight from Mt. Rishyamuka to where Raghavaa-s are.

verses.devanagari:
कपि रूपम् परित्यज्य हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः |
भिक्षु रूपम् ततो भेजे शठबुद्धितया कपिः
verses.iast:
kapi rūpam parityajya hanumān mārutātmajaḥ |
bhixu rūpam tato bheje śaṭhabuddhitayā kapiḥ
verses.translation: Casting off his monkey's semblance Air-god's son Hanuma attained the persona of an ascetic, for that monkey is incredulous in mind about Raghava-s.
notes: Sugreeva doubted Rama and Lakshmana to be the mercenaries sent by his elder brother Vali, for kings of that nature will always be on hunt for their enemies. Hence he ordered Hanuma not to approach them in his original persona that is of a mighty monkey, c.f. 4-2-24. This is the reason why he chose the form of ascetic, thinking that nobody tells a lie to an ascetic, and thus he wanted to gain information in an ascetic's form, but futile is his effort. Rama or Lakshmana will go on listening to what Hanuma says, without any reply. Hanuma himself is vexed at their silence and he has to come out of his guise to reveal his original form, as at 4-3-19.

verses.devanagari:
ततः च हनुमान् वाचा श्लक्ष्णया सुमनोज्ञया |
विनीतवत् उपागम्य राघवौ प्रणिपत्य च
अबभाषे च तौ वीरौ यथावत् प्रशशंस च |
verses.iast:
tataḥ ca hanumān vācā ślakṣṇayā sumanojñayā |
vinītavat upāgamya rāghavau praṇipatya ca
ababhāṣe ca tau vīrau yathāvat praśaśaṃsa ca |
verses.translation: Then on nearing Raghava-s that Hanuma voicing softly and well pleasingly like an obedient one, that best monkey befittingly hailed, greeted and praised those two valiant ones.

glosses.meaning: greeted them [not talking exactly,] also, to those two, valiant ones

verses.devanagari:
संपूज्य विधिवद् वीरौ हनुमान् वानरोत्तमः
उवाच कामतो वाक्यम् मृदु सत्य पराक्रमौ |
verses.iast:
sampūjya vidhivad vīrau hanumān vānarottamaḥ
uvāca kāmato vākyam mṛdu satya parākramau |
verses.translation: The best Vanara Hanuma spoke soft-wordily, as desired by Sugreeva, to those candidly resolute ones, on making reverent obeisance to both of them.

glosses.meaning: to both candid, resolutely, valorous ones

verses.devanagari:
राजर्षि देव प्रतिमौ तापसौ संशित व्रतौ
देशम् कथम् इमम् प्राप्तौ भवन्तौ वर वर्णिनौ |
त्रासयन्तौ मृग गणान् अन्याम् च वन चारिणः
verses.iast:
rājarṣi deva pratimau tāpasau saṃśita vratau
deśam katham imam prāptau bhavantau vara varṇinau |
trāsayantau mṛga gaṇān anyām ca vana cāriṇaḥ
verses.translation: "You two look like kingly saints, or deities by your build, ascetics with blest vows, but with ideal complexions... how come you arrived at this countryside scaring the herds of animals and other inhabitants of this forest...

glosses.meaning: animal, herds of, other inhabitants, scaring

verses.devanagari:
पम्पा तीर रुहान् वृक्षान् वीक्षमाणौ समंततः |
इमाम् नदीम् शुभ जलाम् शोभयन्तौ तरस्विनौ
धैर्यवन्तौ सुवर्णाभौ कौ युवाम् चीर वाससौ |
निःश्वसन्तौ वर भुजौ पीडयन्तौ इमाः प्रजाः
verses.iast:
pampā tīra ruhān vṛkṣān vīkṣamāṇau samaṃtataḥ |
imām nadīm śubha jalām śobhayantau tarasvinau
dhairyavantau suvarṇābhau kau yuvām cīra vāsasau |
niḥśvasantau vara bhujau pīḍayantau imāḥ prajāḥ
verses.translation: "You mighty ones you are watching the trees grown on the banks of Pampa from all over, and owing to your presence on these banks you make this river Pampa with its propitious waters to shine forth... but you with your golden hue appear as courageous ones, yet you sigh over repeatedly, you wear jute-cloths, yet you look mighty shouldered... who are you that distress all the beings in this forest...

glosses.meaning: this one, the river, make to shine

verses.devanagari:
सिंह विप्रेक्षितौ वीरौ महाबल पराक्रमौ |
शक्र चाप निभे चापे गृहीत्वा शत्रु नाशनौ
श्रीमन्तौ रूप संपन्नौ वृषभ श्रेष्ठ विक्रमौ |
हस्ति हस्त उपम भुजौ द्युतिमन्तौ नरर्षभौ
verses.iast:
siṃha viprekṣitau vīrau mahābala parākramau |
śakra cāpa nibhe cāpe gṛhītvā śatru nāśanau
śrīmantau rūpa sampannau vṛṣabha śreṣṭha vikramau |
hasti hasta upama bhujau dyutimantau nararṣabhau
verses.translation: "Dauntless, bold and brave are you with sharp glances of lions, wielding bows like that of Indra's bow you are the real enemy destroyers... glorious, splendid, and even impetuous you appear like Sacred Bulls... elephant's trunks are your arms... and you foremost among men are self-resplendent...

verses.devanagari:
प्रभया पर्वत इन्द्रः असौ युवयोः अवभासितः |
राज्य अर्हौ अमर प्रख्यौ कथम् देशम् इह आगतौ
verses.iast:
prabhayā parvata indraḥ asau yuvayoḥ avabhāsitaḥ |
rājya arhau amara prakhyau katham deśam iha āgatau
verses.translation: "This lord-like mountain is effulgent with your effulgence, you two look as kingdom-worthy, or worthy divinities, but how you have reached this countryside now...

glosses.meaning: now, to country-side, how, you reached.

verses.devanagari:
पद्म पत्र ईक्षणौ वीरौ जटा मण्डल धारिणौ |
अन्योन्य सदृशौ वीरौ देव लोकात् इह आगतौ
यदृच्छयेव संप्राप्तौ चन्द्र सूर्यौ वसुंधराम् |
विशाल वक्षसौ वीरौ मानुषौ देव रूपिणौ
सिंह स्कन्धौ महा उत्साहौ समदौ इव गोवृषौ |
verses.iast:
padma patra īkṣaṇau vīrau jaṭā maṇḍala dhāriṇau |
anyonya sadṛśau vīrau deva lokāt iha āgatau
yadṛcchayeva samprāptau candra sūryau vasuṃdharām |
viśāla vakṣasau vīrau mānuṣau deva rūpiṇau
siṃha skandhau mahā utsāhau samadau iva govṛṣau |
verses.translation: "Eyes of yours are like fine lotus petals, are you superhuman... nay, you wear tufts and braids, are you some undaunted human ascetics... nay, you look clonal, are you from some world of gods... nay, you are on earth, does this earth have a chance to receive Sun and Moon on her by her fortune... nay, are you some broad-chested deities in human form... lion-shouldered, very vehement and vigorous like Sacred Bulls... who you might be...

glosses.meaning: steadfast ones, from gods', world, hither, arrived

verses.devanagari:
आयताः च सुवृत्ताः च बाहवः परिघोपमाः
सर्व भूषण भूषार्हाः किम् अर्थम् न विभूषिताः |
verses.iast:
āyatāḥ ca suvṛttāḥ ca bāhavaḥ parighopamāḥ
sarva bhūṣaṇa bhūṣārhāḥ kim artham na vibhūṣitāḥ |
verses.translation: "Also lengthy are your hands, and spherical are your shoulders similar to clubs... they are worthy for decoration with every kind of ornament, for what reason they are undecorated...
notes: Here in the verse plural number is used for hands, āyatāḥ, bāhavaḥ, parighāḥ, whereas so far, dual number, dvivacana is used to describe any two. The ancient commentators take this as many hands, more than two, as opposite to other dual numbered wording. For this it is said that since Lakshmana is a right hand to Rama, Hanuma sees a three-handed god in Rama. But Hanuma is talking to both Rama and Lakshmana; there shall be two deities with two hands each. The accepted phenomenon is that, Hanuma as a true devotee has seen the fourhanded Vishnu in Rama. This is according to Govindaraja. Next, the arms of Rama are of protective nature to the friendly ones. āyātāḥ, lengthily ones - they can be stretched to any extent, and on the other hand, anything can depend on them, as in yopām āyatanam veda... and this su vrittaaH, round like the serpent's hoods, or body builder's clubs, is to tell that no one can near them. Thus, the spherical universe can depend on the spherical shoulders of Rama. Thus Hanuma is reminding Rama of his wild-boar incarnation where the whole world is lifted on his snout from waters. The word parighaḥ, is to say that those spherical shoulders can remove difficulties of those who adore them. The parighaḥ in simple terms means, clubs, bludgeon, or ancient dumbbell unlike the present day dumbbells of gym, but the word is deciphered to be pari gha fully, removing, or fully, falling to one's lot. That is, here these shoulders are mighty to eliminate Vali and these hands if shook by Sugreeva in friendship, Sugreeva's miseries will be removed completely.

glosses.meaning: for all kinds of, ornaments, decor-worthy

verses.devanagari:
उभौ योग्यौ अहम् मन्ये रक्षितुम् पृथिवीम् इमाम्
स सागर वनाम् कृत्स्नाम् विन्ध्य मेरु विभूषिताम् |
verses.iast:
ubhau yogyau aham manye rakṣitum pṛthivīm imām
sa sāgara vanām kṛtsnām vindhya meru vibhūṣitām |
verses.translation: "I deem that each of you are the choicest one to protect the earth adorned with Mt Meru and Vindhya range, and with all her oceans and forests...

glosses.meaning: Mt. Vindhya, Mt. Meru, adorned with
entire, earth, to protect, choicest one.

verses.devanagari:
इमे च धनुषी चित्रे श्लक्ष्णे चित्र अनुलेपने
प्रकाशेते यथा इन्द्रस्य वज्रे हेम विभूषिते |
verses.iast:
ime ca dhanuṣī citre ślakṣṇe citra anulepane
prakāśete yathā indrasya vajre hema vibhūṣite |
verses.translation: "And these awesome bows are polished with odd things are smooth, and they are brightening like the gilded Thunderbolt of Indra.

verses.devanagari:
संपूर्णाः च शितैः बाणैः तूणाः च शुभ दर्शनाः
जीवित अन्तकरैः घोरैः ज्वलद्भिः इव पन्नगैः |
verses.iast:
sampūrṇāḥ ca śitaiḥ bāṇaiḥ tūṇāḥ ca śubha darśanāḥ
jīvita antakaraiḥ ghoraiḥ jvaladbhiḥ iva pannagaiḥ |
verses.translation: "Full with hazardous, life terminating, fiery snake like sharp arrows are these quivers, admirable in their appearance...

verses.devanagari:
महा प्रमाणौ विपुलौ तप्त हाटक भूषणौ
खड्गौ एतौ विराजेते निर्मुक्त भुजगौ इव |
verses.iast:
mahā pramāṇau vipulau tapta hāṭaka bhūṣaṇau
khaḍgau etau virājete nirmuk{}ta bhujagau iva |
verses.translation: "Dazzling are these amply wide, broad and gilded swords like the snakes just released from their moults...

verses.devanagari:
एवम् माम् परिभाषन्तम् कस्माद् वै न अभि भाषतः
सुग्रीवो नाम धर्मात्मा कश्चित् वानर पुंगवः |
वीरो विनिकृतो भ्रात्रा जगत् भ्रमति दुःखितः
verses.iast:
evam mām paribhāṣantam kasmād vai na abhi bhāṣataḥ
sugrīvo nāma dharmātmā kaścit vānara puṃgavaḥ |
vīro vinikṛto bhrātrā jagat bhramati duḥkhitaḥ
verses.translation: "When I have been talking to you this way, what for you don't speak up... one named Sugreeva, somebody virtuous and worthily one among monkeys is expelled by his brother Vali, and he is roaming all over the world sorrowfully...
notes: A monkey cannot be teased this far, for it will show its teeth, if exceeded. Hanuma is vexed with their silence. So far he has been talking all flattering words, which he has drawn from many scriptures, i.e., scriptures. Their apparels and hair tufts are like those of sages and hermits, along with their self-contradictory resemblance as would-have-been emperors, and their mighty weaponry, and every other thing he said are the quotes from lakshana shaatra, the scripture that prescribes the qualities of great emperors. This is what the other two listeners are assessing about the questioner also. In the midst of this unpopulated thick forest, some ascetic comes in, talks at length, that too without offence to the scriptures, is the doubt of those two brothers. This particular questioner is not definitely any ascetic or sage, because he is roaming in deep forests, rather than around some villages where he may get some charities. And also that, generally ascetics will talk, only when they are talked to, but this one with some purpose behind, is almost pestering to reveal the identity of the intruders. Hence the brothers took Hanuma to be another demon or anyone sent by somebody, for they already knew about the Vali-Sugreeva episode. Apart from this, Rama is following his own Imperial protocol of assessing the person approaching on his own, who is talking like this one, and who has high knowledge of all the scriptures. This analysis, Rama gives to Lakshmana after a few more verses. For now, Hanuma had to yield to high resistance from those two brothers, and is going to reveal himself, with a come-what-may attitude.

verses.devanagari:
प्राप्तः अहम् प्रेषितः तेन सुग्रीवेण महात्मना |
राज्ञा वानर मुख्यानाम् हनुमान् नाम वानरः
verses.iast:
prāptaḥ aham preṣitaḥ tena sugrīveṇa mahātmanā |
rājñā vānara mukhyānām hanumān nāma vānaraḥ
verses.translation: "Delegated by that great soul and the king of important monkeys Sugreeva, I have come here and by name I am Hanuma, another Vanara...

glosses.meaning: monkeys, of important ones, by king

verses.devanagari:
युवाभ्याम् स हि धर्मात्मा सुग्रीवः सख्यम् इच्छति |
तस्य माम् सचिवम् वित्तम् वानरम् पवनात्मजम्
भिक्षु रूप प्रति च्छन्नम् सुग्रीव प्रिय कारणात् |
ऋश्यमूकात् इह प्राप्तम् कामगम् कामचारिणम्
verses.iast:
yuvābhyām sa hi dharmātmā sugrīvaḥ sakhyam icchati |
tasya mām sacivam vittam vānaram pavanātmajam
bhikṣu rūpa prati cchannam sugrīva priya kāraṇāt |
ṛśyamūkāt iha prāptam kāmagam kāmacāriṇam
verses.translation: "He that righteous Sugreeva is desiring friendship with you two, and know me as a monkey and his minister, the son of Air-god... I had to come here from Mt. Rishyamuka in an ascetic's form only to appease that Sugreeva, and I can wend my way by my will, and wear any guise as I wish..." Hanuma said so to those brothers.

glosses.meaning: with you two, friendship, desiring, indeed
Sugreeva, to appease, by reason of
from Mt. Rishyamuka, here, I reached
by wish, wend, by wish, guise alter
son of, Air-god, a monkey [thus you may know me.]

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्त्वा तु हनुमाम् तौ वीरौ राम लक्ष्मणौ |
वाक्यज्ञो वाक्य कुशलः पुनः न उवाच किंचन
verses.iast:
evam uk{}tvā tu hanumām tau vīrau rāma lakṣmaṇau |
vākyajño vākya kuśalaḥ punaḥ na uvāca kiñcana
verses.translation: Saying thus to those valorous Rama and Lakshmana, Hanumaan, the sententious wordsmith, spoke nothing further.

verses.devanagari:
एतत् श्रुत्वा वचः तस्य रामो लक्ष्मणम् अब्रवीत् |
प्रहृष्ट वदनः श्रीमान् भ्रातरम् पार्श्वतः स्थितम्
verses.iast:
etat śrutvā vacaḥ tasya rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt |
prahṛṣṭa vadanaḥ śrīmān bhrātaram pārśvataḥ sthitam
verses.translation: Hearing all those words said by Hanuma, that illustrious Rama is well pleased facially, spoke to his brother Lakshmana who is standing at his side.
notes: Again Rama is following his imperial protocol. As an emperor he does not enter into any direct conversation with envoys or ambassadors. Later Rama asks Lakshmana to conduct the dialogue with Hanuma. This is said to have another reason. Because Lakshmana is another wordsmith, equalling Hanuma by way of his knowledge in scriptures, Rama assigns that duty to Lakshmana. Now Rama's analysis of this envoy's knowledge, thereby gauging his master's virtuousness, is made know to Lakshmana in the following verses.

glosses.meaning: his, all those, words, on hearing
to his brother, to Lakshmana, spoke.

verses.devanagari:
सचिवो अयम् कपीन्द्रस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः |
तम् एव काङ्क्षमाणस्य मम अन्तिकम् इह आगतः
verses.iast:
sacivo ayam kapīndrasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ |
tam eva kāñkṣamāṇasya mama antikam iha āgataḥ
verses.translation: "He is the minister of that noteworthy soul and king of monkeys, Sugreeva... whom alone I cherish, but he himself has drew nigh of me, on his own...

glosses.meaning: monkey's king's, noteworthy soul, Sugreeva's, minister

glosses.itrans: tam eva kaankshamaaNasya mama antikam upaagataH
glosses.iast: tam eva kānkśamāṇasya mama antikam upāgataḥ
glosses.devanagari: तं एव कान्क्शमाणस्य मम अन्तिकं उपागतः
glosses.meaning: him, alone, [I am] cherishing, at my, near, he arrived.

verses.devanagari:
तम् अभ्यभाष सौमित्रे सुग्रीव सचिवम् कपिम् |
वाक्यज्ञम् मधुरैः वाक्यैः स्नेह युक्तम् अरिन्दम
verses.iast:
tam abhyabhāṣa saumitre sugrīva sacivam kapim |
vākyajñam madhuraiḥ vākyaiḥ sneha yuk{}tam arindama
verses.translation: "Soumitri, with this minister of Sugreeva, the knower of sententiousness and a pleasant worded one, and one with friendliness you exchange pleasantries with that enemy destroyer Hanuma...
notes: The word arindamam meaning 'to the enemy destroyer' is to pertain to Lakshmana as oh, enemy destroyer, because Rama has not yet concluded on Hanuma's epithets. In Chaukambha version, in Gorakhpur version and in Eastern versions it is arindama , in vocative case only, but Baroda and Tokunaga versions and some more have this as arindamam, objective case. Similar usage can be found in this chapter at 4-3-36, vājyajñaḥ, vākyajñam etc.

verses.devanagari:
न अन् ऋग्वेद विनीतस्य न अ\-\-यजुर्वेद धारिणः |
न अ\-\-साम वेद विदुषः शक्यम् एवम् विभाषितुम्
verses.iast:
na an ṛgveda vinītasya na a\-\-yajurveda dhāriṇaḥ |
na a\-\-sāma veda viduṣaḥ śakyam evam vibhāṣitum
verses.translation: "Nay...the non-knower of Rig Veda, or the non-rememberer of Yajur Veda, or the non-scholar of Saama Veda... can possibly, or truly speak this way...
notes: From hereon Rama's analysis of Hanuma is depicted. In Rig Veda every letter has too many phonetically deflected variations, in many ways to mean many things. It is practically impossible to contain that knowledge, unless the recitalist has complete control over it. Hence the word, vinīta , 'well trained' is used. In Yajurveda many anuvāka-s or passages occur recursively, with different utilisation. Remembering not to mix one with the other is a difficult process. Hence the recitalist has to have enormous remembrance. In Saamaveda the pitch and duration of the rendering is of high importance, as such it requires a scholarly bent to control vocal notes. The three words, vinaya, schooling; dhāraṇa, remembrance and vedana knowledge are required to each of the above Veda-s. Atharva Veda, on the other hand, has no recital performance other than the above. Hence, it is said, is not quoted by Rama. Hanuma said 'you two are eligible to rule the earth' as at 4-3-15, which tantamount to the quote brhamā vā idam ekaeva agra āsīt... from Rigveda aitereya. Next he said that you are deities inhuman form at 4-3-13, which has its bearing on the Yajurveda quote ajāyamāno bahudhā vijāyate... Then Rama is said having lotus-petal like eyes, at 4-3-11, taking clue from cChandogya of Saamaveda, myathākapyāsam punḍarīkam evākśiṇī.... Hence these utterances of Hanuman are said to have direct base in the Veda-s.

verses.devanagari:
नूनम् व्यकरणम् कृत्स्नम् अनेन बहुधा श्रुतम् |
बहु व्याहरता अनेन न किंचित् अप शब्दितम्
verses.iast:
nūnam vyakaraṇam kṛtsnam anena bahudhā śrutam |
bahu vyāharatā anena na kiñcit apa śabditam
verses.translation: "Definitely grammar is severally and comprehensively learnt by him... and though much is said by him not a single word has gone amiss of verbiage...
notes: Earlier Vedic knowledge of Hanuma is analysed. Now his knowledge of grammar, the essential part of Vedic learning is analysed. Without the knowledge of subsidiary scriptures of Veda-s, like, vyākarana, nirukta, sikhśa,candas , the study of Vedas and its ancillaries itself is futile. Reading and reciting the Vedic hymns is of no use in practical life, for the knowledge learnt thereon is to be implemented in society. A simple recitalist is known as cāṃdasa orthodox fellow, while the user of that knowledge for the good of society is vyavahārta practical fellow. Hence Hanuma is implementing the grammar and training received originally as a Vedic scholar, because he is a practical one.

verses.devanagari:
न मुखे नेत्रयोः च अपि ललाटे च भ्रुवोः तथा |
अन्येषु अपि च सर्वेषु दोषः संविदितः क्वचित्
verses.iast:
na mukhe netrayoḥ ca api lalāṭe ca bhruvoḥ tathā |
anyeṣu api ca sarveṣu doṣaḥ saṃviditaḥ kvacit
verses.translation: "On his face or eyes, or on forehead or brows, or on other faculties of expression no fault is found...even at the least...
notes: Now the behavioural niceties of a Vedic scholar are being analysed. The sikśa part of Veda-s imposes certain rules while reciting the hymns. There will be some pāṭaka athama-s, Reciters, the worst. The following verse elucidates the skills of such worst reciters.

glosses.meaning: on face, in eyes, or even
in all [faculties,] at the least, fault, is not, found.

verses.devanagari:
अविस्तरम् असंदिग्धम् अविलम्बितम् अव्यथम् |
उरःस्थम् कण्ठगम् वाक्यम् वर्तते मध्यमे स्वरम्
verses.iast:
avistaram asaṃdigdham avilambitam avyatham |
uraḥstham kaṇṭhagam vākyam vartate madhyame svaram
verses.translation: "Unexpanded, un-doubtful, un-delaying and non-dissonant is the tenor of his speech, and it comports in his chest or throat in a medium tone...
notes: After elucidating the reciters, the worst, now the recitation, the worst is being analysed.

verses.devanagari:
संस्कार क्रम संपन्नाम् अद्भुताम् अविलम्बिताम् |
उच्चारयति कल्याणीम् वाचम् हृदय हर्षिणीम्
verses.iast:
saṃskāra krama sampannām adbhutām avilambitām |
uccārayati kalyāṇīm vācam hṛdaya harṣiṇīm
verses.translation: "He has orderly refinement in speech that is remarkable and un-delaying, and he speaks propitious words that are heart-pleasing...
notes: Best reciters will render phonetics as below, as contained in sīkhśa of Veda-s:

verses.devanagari:
अनया चित्रया वाचा त्रिस्थान व्यंजनस्थयाः |
कस्य न आराध्यते चित्तम् उद्यत् असे अरेः अपि
verses.iast:
anayā citrayā vācā tristhāna vyaṃjanasthayāḥ |
kasya na ārādhyate cittam udyat ase areḥ api
verses.translation: "His speech is generated in three places is enthralling... and whose heart is it that is disenchanted, even that of an enemy after raising his sword at him, on hearing his speech...
notes: Three places to generate speech are uraśi at chest, śiraśi at head, kanṭha at throat. A real speqker of his mind has to generate his speech in these three areas, without rendering any lip service. Again this is the rule of Vedic sikśa namely the training.

glosses.meaning: who, not, adores, by heart [whose heart does not become enchanted]
raised, sword, of enemy, even [even an enemy, after raising his sword.]

verses.devanagari:
एवम् विधो यस्य दूतो न भवेत् पार्थिवस्य तु |
सिद्ध्यन्ति हि कथम् तस्य कार्याणाम् गतयोऽनघ
verses.iast:
evam vidho yasya dūto na bhavet pārthivasya tu |
siddhyanti hi katham tasya kāryāṇām gatayo'nagha
verses.translation: "Oh, faultless Lakshmana, if this sort of envoy is not there to a king, really how can that king accomplishes his ways and means...

glosses.meaning: emissary, this kind of, not, going to be
his, works [means,] ways, how, they will accomplish.

verses.devanagari:
एवम् गुण गणैर् युक्ता यस्य स्युः कार्य साधकाः |
तस्य सिद्ध्यन्ति सर्वेऽर्था दूत वाक्य प्रचोदिताः
verses.iast:
evam guṇa gaṇair yuk{}tā yasya syuḥ kārya sādhakāḥ |
tasya siddhyanti sarve'rthā dūta vākya pracoditāḥ
verses.translation: "Should a king have this kind of work accomplishers with a variety of virtues, all his objectives will be achieved impelled by such an envoy's words..." Rama thus said to Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: this kind of, virtue, varieties of, having

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्तः तु सौमित्रिः सुग्रीव सचिवम् कपिम् |
अभ्यभाषत वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यज्ञम् पवनात्मजम्
verses.iast:
evam uk{}taḥ tu saumitriḥ sugrīva sacivam kapim |
abhyabhāṣata vākyajño vākyajñam pavanātmajam
verses.translation: When said thus by Rama, wise-worded Lakshmana spoke to that monkey and the minister of Sugreeva, namely Hanuma, the son of Air-god, who is equally a wise-worded one.

verses.devanagari:
विदिता नौ गुणा विद्वन् सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः |
तम् एव च अवाम् मार्गावः सुग्रीवम् प्लवगेश्वरम्
verses.iast:
viditā nau guṇā vidvan sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ |
tam eva ca avām mārgāvaḥ sugrīvam plavageśvaram
verses.translation: "The virtues of that great soul Sugreeva are known to us, oh, scholarly monkey, we for our part are in search of that lord of fly-jumpers Sugreeva alone...

glosses.meaning: virtues, are known, to both of us
him, that fly-jumpers, lord of, Sugreeva, alone.

verses.devanagari:
यथा ब्रवीषि हनुमान् सुग्रीव वचनाद् इह |
तत् तथा हि करिष्यावो वचनात् तव सत्तम
verses.iast:
yathā bravīṣi hanumān sugrīva vacanād iha |
tat tathā hi kariṣyāvo vacanāt tava sattama
verses.translation: "As you communicated the words of Sugreeva, oh, gentle Hanuma, by them and by your words we indeed wish to do accordingly...

glosses.meaning: like that, we wish to do, indeed.

verses.devanagari:
तत् तस्य वाक्यम् निपुणम् निशम्य
प्रहृष्ट रूपः पवनात्मजः कपिः |
मनः समाधाय जय उपपत्तौ
सख्यम् तदा कर्तुम् इयेष ताभ्याम्
verses.iast:
tat tasya vākyam nipuṇam niśamya
prahṛṣṭa rūpaḥ pavanātmajaḥ kapiḥ |
manaḥ samādhāya jaya upapattau
sakhyam tadā kartum iyeṣa tābhyām
verses.translation: On observing that operative sentence of Lakshmana the monkey Hanuma is gladdened, as seen from his composure, and kept his mind at ease at the prospective victory, and then he wished to materialise the pact of friendship between Rama ad Sugreeva, at the earliest.

glosses.meaning: his [Lakshmana's,] operative, that, sentence, on observing
then, to them, friendship, to materialise [at the earliest,] he wished to.
